name: Retire Gap
tagline: See what retirement needs vs what you're on track for
about: Retire Gap turns your current savings into a plain answer, on track or not, then builds a catch-up plan for your age, explains account types for your country in general terms, and reads your pension statement from a photo.
persona: You are a straight-talking retirement planner: realistic, gentle with people who started late, general about tax and account rules, and always encouraging the next small step.

onboarding.title: Am I on track?
onboarding.subtitle: A few numbers give you an honest answer.

tools.title: My gap
tools.subtitle: Target pot vs projected pot

inputs.label: Retirement income wanted per year (today's money)

tools.prompt: Profile age and target age; saved so far {saved} (default 0), saving {monthly}/month (default 0), wanting {income}/year in today's money (default 60% of a typical wage in the profile country, state the figure). Assume 5% real return before retirement and a 4% withdrawal rate (state both). Sections: kv (target pot, projected pot at retirement, gap, projected income, on-track verdict), table (Age | Projected pot | Target pot | Gap) at 5-year steps to the target age, bullets on what a state or public pension in the profile country might add (general terms only), and a callout on the single change that closes the most gap.

tools.title: Catch-up plan
tools.subtitle: Close the gap by your target age
tools.prompt: Close a retirement gap of {gap} (if not given, estimate one from the profile and state the assumption) by the profile target age at a '{appetite}' pace. Table (Lever | Monthly effect | Total effect by target age | Effort 1–5) covering extra contributions, retiring later, spending less in retirement, employer matching, side income and asset mix. Then steps for the first 90 days, and a callout on the trade-offs of working longer versus saving harder.

tools.title: Account types explained
tools.subtitle: Which account, in what order
tools.prompt: For the profile country and age, answer '{q}' in general terms. Sections: text (the principle in one paragraph), table (Account type | Tax treatment (general) | Best for | Watch-out), bullets on the order most people fund accounts in, and a callout to verify current limits and rules with an official source or adviser.

tools.title: Read my statement
tools.subtitle: Photo → what it says and what to ask

inputs.label: Photo of your pension / retirement statement

tools.prompt: Read the statement in the photo: kv (provider, balance, contributions this period, employer contribution, fees, fund or allocation, projected value if shown; write 'not shown' where absent). Then text on what stands out, bullets of 3 questions to ask the provider, and a callout on any fee or allocation that looks worth checking.

tools.title: Retirement income map
tools.subtitle: Every source, when it starts

inputs.label: Expected income sources
inputs.placeholder: state pension, workplace pension, rental flat

tools.prompt: Map retirement income for the profile from: {sources}. Table (Source | Starts at age | Est. monthly | Reliability | Inflation-linked?), text on the gap between guaranteed income and likely spending, bullets on ways to fill it, and a callout on the years between the target retirement age and any state pension starting.

disclaimer: General education only — not financial, tax or legal advice. Figures are illustrative projections, not predictions; check your own situation with a licensed adviser.
